title: Company Profile & Onboarding
markdown:
**What it is:** Your company's identity and strategy (mission, market, competitors, financials, and org structure) that grounds everything the Executive says. When you use Open Executive just for yourself, it is your **Business profile** (if you own the business) or **Your work**, with the same sections.

**What it does:**

- **Sets up the Executive from your website and your own words** the first time: give your website, describe your work, optionally attach a deck, one-pager or CV, and it works out the rest. It asks a few quick questions about what's missing, then shows you a filled-in draft: the profile, your team, this year's goals with an owner on each, and departments only if your description already listed people by department.
- Lets you review and edit that draft before anything is saved. Nothing is written until you click **Save and start**. A step-by-step form is linked at the bottom of the setup screen.
- Lets you view and edit every section of the profile any time afterward.
- Feeds this context to all specialists so advice fits *your* company, not a generic one.
- After setup, researches your market and competitors and puts what it finds in your brief, and checks your goals every week.

**How to use:**

*First-time setup*

1. On a new install the app opens setup for you. You can also click **Set up profile →** on the banner on Home, or **Set up company** in the sidebar before a profile exists. Setup opens at `/onboard`, full screen.
2. **Set up your Executive**: optionally enter **Your website** (for example `example.com`). It reads the home page and up to four more pages on the same site, such as About, Team and Products, and drafts from them. With a website, the box below asks **Anything the website doesn't say?** (your role, this year's goals, anything private). If the site can't be read, the questions open with "I couldn't read *example.com*, so I'll ask instead" and setup carries on from what you wrote. Otherwise describe your work in the box (what you do, who you sell to, roughly how big you are, what you're focused on this year). Optionally click **＋ Attach a one-pager, deck or CV (optional)** (up to 8 files: PDF, Word, Excel, CSV, Markdown or text). Click **Continue** (any one of the website, the box or a file is enough). While it works, the steps show under the button: reading your website and what you wrote, then getting your first question ready. **Skip, I'll answer questions instead** goes straight to the questions. **I'll do this later** takes you to Home, which keeps setup one tap away.
3. Setup works out whether this is **Personal** (just you) or for your **Team** from what you wrote, without asking: Team when you named colleagues at your company, or your website lists your team (it then asks which of them you are), Personal otherwise. For Personal it also keeps the role, title and who you report to that you mentioned.
4. **A few quick questions**: up to four, each with suggested answers. Tap one, type your own and press Enter, or click **Skip**. Every question is optional. Click **Draft it now** to stop early.
5. **Here's** *your company*: the first line says who it's set up for, for example **Set up for your team: Dana, Sam, Priya, Lee**. Click **Change to just me** or **Change to a team** to switch. Edit the profile sections, and **This year**: your goals, each with an owner (**Add a goal**, pick an owner, or ✕ to remove one). For a team, edit **Your team** (**Add person**, remove someone, tick **This is me** on exactly one person). **Departments** appear only when your description already listed people by department. For Personal, enter your own name and title. Check **Your sign-in email**: it's filled in with the account you're signed in with, and it's how the Executive knows the person marked as you is you. If you're setting this up for someone else, enter the email they will sign in with. **Please check** lists anything it guessed. **After you save, I'll** says what happens next.
6. Click **Save and start**, or **Back to questions** to go back to the conversation. Saving takes you to Home, where the getting-started checklist shows what's worth connecting next. Pick how the Executive sounds any time in Settings.

A setup in progress survives a refresh or a closed tab: open setup again and it picks up at the same question or draft. Click **Start over** on the "Picking up where you left off" note to begin again from the description.

To change an earlier answer, click **Edit** next to it under **Your answers** (or under **Built from your answers** on the draft), change it and click **Save and continue**. The questions after it are asked again, or the profile is redrafted if it already has enough. Files you attached to the description are kept.

Prefer filling in fields? Click **Prefer a form? Use the step-by-step version** for a wizard of up to 12 questions (fewer for Personal). Later steps are optional and can be skipped.

*Afterwards*

- Open **Company** in the sidebar and pick the **Company profile** tab. Click **Edit** on a section, make your changes, and click **Save** (or **Cancel**). List fields take one item per line. The sections are **Company Basics**, **Mission & Vision**, **Target Customer**, **Competitive Landscape**, **External Dependencies**, **Strategic Priorities**, **Culture & Values**, **Org Structure** and **Financials**.
- **External Dependencies** holds vendors and tickers. A vendor or ticker named there counts as company data: the Executive starts watching its status page or filings on its own, without asking you first.
- **Re-run setup**, in the **⋯** at the top of the profile, takes you back through the conversation. A re-run keeps your Personal or Team setting. Only the current owner can mark someone else as **This is me** when re-running it, because saving makes that person the owner.
- The help panel (the sparkle button at the top right) can fill in profile sections for you. The section opens with the suggested values and you still click **Save**.

**Who can change it:** anyone signed in can edit the profile sections. Saving setup adds people and makes someone the owner, so once there is an owner only they can hand that role to someone else. The step-by-step form can only be saved by the owner once there is one.

**Example description:** *"We're Northwind Tools — a 40-person B2B SaaS company selling inventory software to independent hardware stores in the US. About $6M ARR, growing 60% a year, Series A last spring. Our main competitors are Stockly and spreadsheets. This year's priorities are launching in Canada and getting net revenue retention above 110%."*

*Note: until a profile exists, Home shows a banner that responses will be generic, with **Set up profile →**.*
